A also carries no blockquote rule (B has a 2px #BFBFBF bar), and A's #/>/backtick markers are min-gray 122 (~#7A) vs B's 158 (~#9E) on the same #F9F9F9 ground — 36 levels louder than they need to be.
gapTheirs: Markers are inline instead of hung, so the text column moves by block type: body starts at x=673, but H1 text at 721 (+48), H2 at 744 (+71), '- ' items at 722 (+49), '1. ' items at 747 (+74) — a 74px swing where A holds every block at 673–675 (3px total deviation). Worse, the blockquote's wrap line falls back to 673 while its first line sits at 721, so the second line juts 48px LEFT of the first; the quote never forms a block.
verdict: A carves a marker gutter and keeps one wall of text at 673px no matter what you type; B lets the marker live in the text column, so adding a second '#' shoves the whole heading 24px right under your cursor and the paragraph you're writing shifts as you mark it up. B's blockquote is the tell: first line indented to 721, wrap line back at 673, a 48px overhang inside a block that has a vertical rule pretending it's a unit. B buys quieter hashes (#9E vs #7A) and a caret you can actually find, and A blows that advantage with a 2px caret in body-text black that collides with the glyph it sits after — but a caret is one fix and a jumping left margin is the whole architecture.

states.name: dark
states.gap: Blockquotes have no containment at all: the quoted paragraph is rgb(28,28,28) at the same size and the same left edge (x=673) as ordinary body text, marked only by a 122-grey '>' sitting 46px out in the gutter — B draws a 4px #494949 rule spanning the full 108px height of the quote block, so in A a quote reads as plain prose at a glance.
states.gapTheirs: No hanging indent — markers sit inline, so nothing shares a left edge: body text starts at x=673, H1 text at 721, H2 text at 744, bullet text at 721, ordered-list text at 747, and the blockquote's second line snaps back from 721 to 676, a 45px (~2 character cell) jump mid-sentence. A hangs every marker in a 24–72px gutter and holds one uninterrupted 673px edge across headings, paragraphs, quote, both list types and every wrap.
states.verdict: A is the only one of the two where you can run your eye down the left margin and see a single straight edge with the syntax pushed out of the way; B's structure is nailed to the text, so headings step right by level, the two list types disagree by 26px, and a wrapped quote line lurches two characters left as you type into it. B buys you a quote rule and a caret you can actually find, but it pays for them by making the text jump — which is the one thing this piece is supposed to prevent. A's failure is the opposite and cheaper: the blockquote is invisible as a blockquote, an omission fixed by one border, while B's is a layout decision baked into every line. Neither app bothers to make a heading any larger than body text, so both are asking a bold weight to carry the entire hierarchy.

B uses two marker greys in one document — #636363 for #/##/> and #808080 for -/1. — while A uses #7A7A7A for every marker including the * and ** pairs
Marker vs text separation: A markers 4.4:1 against #F9F9F9 with body at 15.9:1; B heading/quote markers only 2.6:1 against #1A1A1A, past quiet into barely-there
Headings are body-size in both (24.2px advance, same as prose); no size step at any level

Neither shows any reveal-on-cursor behaviour: raw ** and * stay printed on lines far from the caret in both
